lines.trans: Look closely at this page: it measures decibels and quietness, not hotel stars!
Decibels? So nine out of ten was not a score for my check-in?
Well, your check-in deserves a ten! Actually, though, I am an acoustic architect.

words.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

lines.trans: An acoustic architect! Do you design concert halls?
Small libraries and courtyards, mostly. I measure how old walls block street noise.
That is why you were listening last night for cars up in the attic!
Exactly. Outside on the avenue it is loud, yet inside this courtyard you hear leaves and birds.
Wait until Ernesto hears he panicked all night over decibels!
Truthfully, I also chose this neighbourhood for an old family reason.
Oh? Did your family live near here once?
Two streets from here, when I was little. Friday is... an important day for me.

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Cerca de + noun = near something; de cerca = up close.

examples.trans: My family lives very nearby.
Look closely at this page.

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.
This morning it is very sunny.

meanings.note: La segunda página = page two.

examples.trans: The page is here.

examples.text: Vemos las páginas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pages from the door.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> i: mido, midió).

examples.text: Mido el ancho de la mesa nueva.
examples.trans: I measure the width of the new table.

examples.text: El carpintero midió la tabla dos veces.
examples.trans: The carpenter measured the plank twice.

meanings.note: Unit for measuring sound volume.

examples.trans: The decibel is here.

examples.text: Vemos los decibelios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the decibels from the door.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.
It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: En silencio = quietly.

examples.text: El silencio es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The silence is very important here.
We talk about the silence.

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

meanings.note: De cinco estrellas = five-star.

examples.trans: The star is here.

examples.text: Vemos las estrellas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stars from the door.

meanings.note: Plural los hoteles.

examples.trans: The hotel is here.

examples.text: Vemos los hoteles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the hotels from the door.

meanings.note: Desde entonces = since then.

examples.text: ¿Entonces nos vemos mañana a las ocho?
examples.trans: So shall we see each other tomorrow at eight?
Since then she works with us.

meanings.note: Las nueve = nine o'clock.

examples.text: El tren llega a las nueve en punto.
examples.trans: The train arrives at nine on the dot.
We saw a nine out of ten.

sobre.gloss: on; upon; about; out of (nueve sobre diez)

meanings.en: on; upon; about; out of (nueve sobre diez)
meanings.note: Sobre todo = above all / mostly; also a homograph noun el sobre ('envelope').

examples.text: Deja la llave sobre el mostrador.
examples.trans: Leave the key on the counter.

examples.text: Sacó nueve sobre diez en la prueba.
examples.trans: She scored nine out of ten on the test.

meanings.note: Diez sobre diez = ten out of ten.

examples.trans: There are ten minutes left before starting.
Your front desk deserves a ten.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.
That blue suitcase is mine.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Covers jotted notes, musical notes, and review scores.

examples.trans: The note is here.

examples.text: Vemos las notas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the notes from the door.

meanings.note: Plural mis (mi llave / mis llaves); unaccented, distinct from pronoun mí.

examples.trans: My suitcase is navy blue.

examples.text: Mis apuntes están en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: My notes are in my pocket.

meanings.note: En recepción = at the front desk.

examples.trans: The front desk is here.

examples.text: Vemos las recepciones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the front desks from the door.

meanings.note: Shortens to buen before masculine singular nouns (buen viaje); ¡Buenos días! = Good morning!

examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!
The weather is very nice today.

su.gloss: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)

meanings.en: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)
meanings.note: Plural sus (su maleta / sus maletas).

examples.trans: Here is your key, madam.

examples.text: Sus habitaciones están en la primera planta.
examples.trans: Your rooms are on the first floor.

meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg merezco.

examples.trans: This coffee deserves five stars.

examples.text: Después de correr, mereces un descanso.
examples.trans: After running, you deserve a rest.

meanings.note: Core contrast conjunction.

examples.text: Hace frío fuera, pero dentro se está bien.
examples.trans: It is cold outside, yet inside it is cosy.

examples.text: Es pequeño, pero tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: It is small, but it has lots of light.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: En realidad softens a correction ('actually / in fact').

examples.text: La realidad es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The reality is very important here.
We talk about the reality.

meanings.note: Feminine: la arquitecta.

examples.trans: The architect is here.

examples.text: Vemos los arquitectos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the architects from the door.

meanings.note: Relating to sound and room acoustics.

examples.trans: It is an acoustic piece.
An acoustic architect! Do you design concert halls?

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.trans: The architect designs quiet libraries.

examples.text: Diseñaron un patio lleno de luz.
examples.trans: They designed a courtyard full of light.

meanings.note: Takes 3rd-person singular verbs (¿quiere usted...?).

examples.trans: What is your name?

examples.text: Pase usted por aquí, por favor.
examples.trans: Come this way, please.

meanings.note: Sala de conciertos = concert hall; sala de la caldera = boiler room.

examples.trans: The hall is here.

examples.text: Vemos las salas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the halls from the door.

meanings.note: Sala de conciertos = concert hall.

examples.trans: The concert is here.

examples.text: Vemos los conciertos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the concerts from the door.

meanings.note: False friend: means 'library', whereas librería means 'bookshop'.

examples.trans: The library is here.

examples.text: Vemos las bibliotecas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the libraries from the door.

meanings.note: Hermano pequeño = younger brother; de pequeño = as a child.

examples.trans: It is a small piece.

examples.text: Hay una pequeña tarjeta de cartón atada al asa.
examples.trans: There is a small cardboard card tied to the handle.

meanings.note: Traditional inner courtyard at the heart of a Spanish building.

examples.trans: The courtyard is here.

examples.text: Vemos los patios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the courtyards from the door.

meanings.note: Todo el día = the whole day; todo el mundo = everyone; sobre todo = mostly.

examples.text: Todo está limpio y en su sitio.
examples.trans: Everything is clean and in its place.

examples.text: Camina todo recto por esta calle.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead down this street.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb with written accent.

examples.trans: What is your name?
How do I find the hardware shop?

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: Exterior or structural masonry wall.

examples.trans: The thick wall is here.

examples.text: Vemos los muros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the thick walls from the door.

meanings.note: Placed after a noun, means 'historic' or 'old-fashioned'.

examples.trans: It is an old piece.

examples.text: Encantada, Tomás, ¡siempre que nadie hable de vender pianos antiguos!
examples.trans: Gladly, Tomas, as long as nobody talks about selling old pianos!

meanings.note: Means both braking a vehicle and stopping noise.

examples.text: El taxi frena suave junto a la acera.
examples.trans: The taxi brakes gently at the curb.

examples.text: Los muros gruesos frenan el ruido.
examples.trans: Thick walls block out the noise.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.
Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Hacer ruido = make noise; hay ruido = it is noisy.

examples.trans: The noise is here.

examples.text: Vemos los ruidos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the noises from the door.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.
The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la calle.

examples.trans: The street is here.

examples.text: Vemos las calles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the streets from the door.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Neuter pronoun; por eso = that is why.

examples.trans: That is why I brought two umbrellas.
What does that mean exactly?

meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'to' before things (escucha el agua).

examples.text: Escucho los pájaros desde mi cama.
examples.trans: I listen to the birds from my bed.

examples.text: Escuchamos la lluvia sobre las tejas.
examples.trans: We listened to the rain on the tiles.

meanings.note: Single word meaning 'last night' (never la última noche).

examples.text: Anoche llovió mucho en la ciudad.
examples.trans: Last night it rained heavily in the city.
Did you sleep well last night?

meanings.note: Unaccented conjunction, distinct from accented sí ('yes').

examples.trans: Let me know if you need another blanket.

examples.text: Mira si queda leche en la nevera.
examples.trans: Check whether any milk is left in the fridge.

pasar.gloss: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen

meanings.en: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen
meanings.note: ¿Qué pasa? = What's wrong?; No pasa nada = No problem.

examples.trans: Come in, please, and have a seat!

examples.text: Pasa la farmacia verde a la derecha.
examples.trans: Pass the green pharmacy on your right.

meanings.note: Standard word in Spain for an automobile.

examples.trans: The car is here.

examples.text: Vemos los coches desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cars from the door.

meanings.note: Opposite of abajo.

examples.trans: The bedrooms are upstairs.
Look up toward the balcony.

meanings.note: Top-floor room with sloping roof beams.

examples.trans: The attic room is here.

examples.text: Vemos las buhardillas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the attic rooms from the door.

meanings.note: Used alone as an enthusiastic 'Exactly!'.

examples.trans: It is an exact piece.

examples.text: ¡Exacto! Ya eres una más del equipo.
examples.trans: Exactly! You are already one of the team.

meanings.note: Por fuera = on the outside.

examples.trans: It is cold outside this morning.

examples.text: La maleta es azul por fuera.
examples.trans: The suitcase is blue on the outside.

meanings.note: Wide main street in a city.

examples.trans: The avenue is here.

examples.text: Vemos las avenidas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the avenues from the door.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.
We have already prepared the rooms.

meanings.note: Agrees before nouns (mucha agua, muchos años); invariable after verbs (llueve mucho).

examples.trans: Today we have a lot of work.
Thank you very much for the coffee.

meanings.note: Dentro de + time means 'in (after) a certain amount of time'.

examples.trans: There are four tables inside.
I will be back in ten minutes.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

meanings.note: Irregular: oigo, oyes, oye, oímos, oís, oyen; ¡Oiga! / ¡Oye! gets someone's attention.

examples.trans: Can you hear me clearly on the phone?

examples.text: Acabo de oír pasos en la escalera.
examples.trans: I just heard footsteps on the stairs.

meanings.note: Means both a tree leaf and a single sheet of paper.

examples.trans: The leaf is here.

examples.text: Vemos las hojas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the leaves from the door.

meanings.note: Garden songbird.

examples.trans: The bird is here.

examples.text: Vemos los pájaros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the birds from the door.

esperar.gloss: to wait; to wait for; to hope

meanings.en: to wait; to wait for; to hope
meanings.note: Covers both 'wait (for)' and 'hope'.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, please.
We hope you rest very well.

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

saber.gloss: to know (a fact / how to); to taste (saber a)

meanings.en: to know (a fact / how to); to taste (saber a)
meanings.note: Irregular: sé, supe; sabe igual que = it tastes just like.

examples.trans: Do you know where the wrench is?

examples.text: Este bizcocho sabe a limón fresco.
examples.trans: This cake tastes of fresh lemon.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb.

examples.text: El dueño sufre por cada pequeño detalle.
examples.trans: The owner frets over every small detail.

examples.text: El tejado no sufrió daños con la tormenta.
examples.trans: The roof suffered no damage in the storm.

meanings.note: ¡Buenas noches! = Good evening / Good night; esta noche = tonight.

examples.trans: The night is here.

examples.text: Vemos las noches desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the nights from the door.

meanings.note: La verdad = honestly / the truth.

examples.trans: The truth is here.

examples.text: Vemos las verdades desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the truths from the door.

meanings.note: Positive counterpart of tampoco.

examples.text: Yo también quiero un trozo de bizcocho.
examples.trans: I want a piece of sponge cake too.
We also have mint tea.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> i: elijo, eligió).

examples.text: Elijo una mesa bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: I choose a table under the tree.

examples.text: Elegimos este barrio por su calma.
examples.trans: We chose this neighbourhood for its calm.

meanings.note: Local city district with its own shops and squares.

examples.trans: The neighbourhood is here.

examples.text: Vemos los barrios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the neighbourhoods from the door.

meanings.note: Before a noun (un viejo amigo), means 'long-standing / dear old'.

examples.trans: It is an old piece.
The old sunny attic room... follow me, quickly!

meanings.note: Un viejo motivo familiar = an old family reason.

examples.trans: The reason is here.

examples.text: Vemos los motivos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the reasons from the door.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.trans: It is a family piece.

examples.text: ¡Qué curioso! La letra de esa etiqueta me resultaba muy familiar.
examples.trans: How curious! The handwriting on that tag felt very familiar to me.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization or understanding.

examples.trans: Ah, now I understand the map!
Oh really? What good news.

meanings.note: Accented sí means 'yes' (distinct from unaccented si = 'if').

examples.trans: Yes, the room is ready.
Of course, come right in!

meanings.note: Takes singular verb agreement in Spanish (la familia vive aquí).

examples.trans: The family is here.

examples.text: Vemos las familias desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the families from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb.

examples.text: Vivo a dos calles de la plaza.
examples.trans: I live two streets from the square.

examples.text: Mis primos vivieron aquí muchos años.
examples.trans: My cousins lived here for many years.

meanings.note: Right where the speaker is.

examples.trans: Here is your key.

examples.text: Nos sentamos aquí bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We sit right here under the tree.

meanings.note: Antes de means 'before' a noun or infinitive.

examples.trans: I arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: Antes de salir, cierra la ventana.
examples.trans: Before leaving, close the window.

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

meanings.note: Unaccented in statements and time clauses (interrogative: cuándo).

examples.trans: Let me know when the taxi arrives.

examples.text: Cuando llueve, huele a tierra mojada.
examples.trans: When it rains, it smells like wet earth.

meanings.note: Often omitted in Spanish unless adding contrast or emphasis.

examples.text: Yo abro la puerta y tú llevas la linterna.
examples.trans: I will open the door and you carry the flashlight.
It is me, please open up.

meanings.note: Invariable in plural: el viernes ('on Friday'), los viernes ('on Fridays').

examples.trans: The Friday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los viernes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Fridays from the door.

meanings.note: Masculine despite ending in -a: el día, ¡Buenos días!.

examples.trans: The day is here.

examples.text: Vemos los días desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the days from the door.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.trans: It is an important piece.

examples.text: A dos calles de aquí, cuando yo era pequeño. El viernes es... un día importante para mí.
examples.trans: Two streets from here, when I was little. Friday is... an important day for me.

meanings.note: Marks destination, recipient (para ti), deadline, and minutes to the hour (cinco para las doce).

examples.text: Este paquete blanco es para mi hermano.
examples.trans: This white parcel is for my brother.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is ten minutes to twelve.

meanings.note: Accented pronoun after para, por, a, de, sin (distinct from possessive mi).

examples.text: Esta taza de té es para mí.
examples.trans: This cup of tea is for me.
Leave it to me, please.

meanings.note: De momento = for now.

examples.trans: The moment is here.

examples.text: Vemos los momentos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the moments from the door.

acabar.gloss: to finish; to have just (acabar de)

meanings.en: to finish; to have just (acabar de)
meanings.note: Acabar de + infinitive means 'to have just done something'.

examples.trans: I have just arrived from the market.

examples.text: Ya acabamos el trabajo de hoy.
examples.trans: We already finished today's work.

meanings.note: Querer decir means 'to mean'.

examples.trans: What does the letter say exactly?
Tell me the truth without fear.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.
We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! is Spain's most common everyday farewell.

examples.text: Cruza el puente y luego gira.
examples.trans: Cross the bridge and then turn.
See you later, have a good day!
